candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether numeric values in the Effluent Conc (Ce) column versus Ambient Conc (Ca), instream waste-concentration derivations (2.13*Ce, Cd,dom, Cd, Cd,hh), or the various use-specific criteria columns are treated as enforceable discharge limits versus background/derivation-only criteria changes which column value is selected as the applicable limit for compliance comparison.

candidates.locator: Page 26, Section: fact_sheet, MQL column header
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of MQL as a reporting/detection threshold versus an enforceable limit, or as evidence of a required monitored parameter, affects whether reported values below MQL trigger numeric exceedance analysis (A), whether monitoring was required for that parameter (B), and how no-result or below-quantitation data should be classified (C).

candidates.locator: Page 26, Section: fact_sheet, Mercury dissolved row
candidates.computation_change_reason: The dissolved-mercury row lists an MQL and several finite aquatic/human-health criteria but leaves Effluent Conc (Ce) blank; different readings of blank Ce as no enforceable effluent limit, as report-only monitoring, or as deferral to another limit source change whether measurements can be compared to a numeric limit (A) and how absent or non-detect results are categorized (C).

candidates.locator: Page 26, Section: fact_sheet, Mercury total row
candidates.computation_change_reason: This row supplies a populated Effluent Conc (Ce = 5.04 ug/l) alongside multiple other numeric criteria (2, 0.77, etc.) and 1E+100 placeholders; choosing Ce versus another column as the operative discharge limit, or treating 1E+100 as non-operative, changes the numeric limit used for exceedance determination and whether dissolved versus total mercury measurements are matched to this row.

candidates.locator: Page 26, Section: fact_sheet, Nickel dissolved (P) row
candidates.computation_change_reason: The parenthetical "(P)" qualifier and the row's populated Ce (0.93922136 ug/l) are ambiguous as to conditional applicability; different readings of (P) as a scope trigger, analyte form selector, or labeling artifact change whether this effluent limit and any associated monitoring obligation apply to a given discharge point or period.

candidates.locator: Page 26, Section: fact_sheet, Selenium dissolved (P) row
candidates.computation_change_reason: This row has no populated Ce but lists finite use-specific criteria (50, 130, 4200) and carries a "(P)" qualifier; interpreting whether dissolved selenium is subject to an effluent limit here, only to ambient/use criteria, or only under the (P) condition changes applicable limit selection (A) and whether dissolved-selenium monitoring was required (B).

candidates.locator: Page 26, Section: fact_sheet, Selenium dis (SO4 >500 mg/l) row
candidates.computation_change_reason: The row title embeds an explicit sulfate-condition trigger (SO4 >500 mg/l) and differs from the adjacent dissolved-selenium row in criteria values (e.g., 250 vs 130 irrigation criterion); whether that condition is met determines if this alternate limit/monitoring regime applies (A,B) and how missing selenium results should be interpreted when sulfate data are absent or borderline (C).

candidates.locator: Page 26, Section: fact_sheet, Selenium total recoverable row
candidates.computation_change_reason: A separate total-recoverable selenium row with Ce = 1.5 ug/l coexists with dissolved-selenium rows; interpretation of which form is required for monitoring and which Ce or criteria column governs compliance changes limit applicability and monitoring obligation for reported dissolved versus total selenium measurements.

candidates.locator: Page 26, Section: fact_sheet, Thalllium dissolved (P) row
candidates.computation_change_reason: Blank Ce alongside a finite Human Health Criteria value (0.47 ug/l) and a "(P)" qualifier creates ambiguity over whether thallium has an enforceable effluent limit in this table, only a human-health criterion, or a conditionally applicable requirement; that choice changes limit selection (A) and monitoring applicability (B).

candidates.locator: Page 26, Section: fact_sheet, 1E+100 sentinel values (example: Molybdenum dissolved row)
candidates.computation_change_reason: Repeated 1E+100 entries appear where other rows carry finite criteria; treating 1E+100 as meaning no numeric criterion versus a literal cap changes whether numeric compliance comparison is applicable for those columns (A) and whether missing data should be classified as non-comparable/report-only rather than a compliance gap (C).

Very small Ce and derived criteria values (e.g., 0.0000124 ug/l Ce versus 5.1E-08 human-health criterion) raise interpretive ambiguity over unit scaling, significant figures, and which column supplies the enforceable limit, which would change exceedance outcomes for reported dioxin measurements.

candidates.locator: Page 26, Section: fact_sheet, Need TMDL column header and values
candidates.computation_change_reason: The Need TMDL column appears for each pollutant row (all shown as N/A in this segment); interpreting N/A as confirming no TMDL-driven limit override versus as unknown or not assessed affects whether TMDL-related limits or additional monitoring obligations are considered applicable.
